You got me interested into this vanity coin thing, so I finally compiled vanitygen from the source I had lying around (available at https://github.com/samr7/vanitygen)) and tried it out. Had to run "sudo apt-get install libssl-dev" first, as I was missing headers, and then just follow it by "make" - and there it was!

Told it to generate an address starting with "1heLLo" (you know, there are these unfortunate limitations forbidding use of certain characters, like O,0,l,I and few others).

It set to work and puffed for about 2 hours on my i3 laptop. And then I had the address and the private key. :)

So, turns out, it is very easy to create vanity coins (addresses, to be precise). Try it yourself.

The number of predefined characters obviously affects the time it takes to generate the address though, so it may take some time on RPi, but it being small it probably does not matter much, if you automate it, switch it on and forget about it for a month.
